subject: Post-demo: Private VPC connectivity recap & next asks
messages:
From: Sean Gallagher <sean_gallagher@redwood.com>
To: Alex Monroe <amonroe@datafoundry.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>, Dev Patel <dev_patel@redwood.com>
Date: Fri, 02 Apr 2027 15:30:00 -0700
Subject: Post-demo: Private VPC connectivity recap & next asks

Alex — thanks for taking the time today. Quick recap from our call and the network-related asks to keep momentum: 

Summary
- DataFoundry prefers private connectivity for sensitive ML inference (understandable).
- We reviewed deployment options: Hosted API (fast), Dedicated (reserved GPU pool), Private VPC (VPC peering or PrivateLink). Your team indicated PrivateLink as the preferred option if it meets routing constraints.

Action items for DataFoundry (please confirm by EOD Monday):
1) Confirm preferred connectivity type: PrivateLink (preferred) or VPC peering.
2) Provide AWS account ID(s) for endpoint creation and the public IP ranges your egress will come from (or NAT config).
3) Share the subnet CIDRs where the PrivateLink endpoint will live and whether cross-account endpoints are acceptable.
4) Point of contact for NetOps (name + email + calendar availability next week).

What we’ll do on our side:
- Prepare a connectivity checklist and a draft network diagram for your review (I’ll attach a Redwood-side checklist).
- If PrivateLink: we’ll generate the VPCE service and share the service name and required security group rules.
- If peering: we’ll outline required route table entries, allowed CIDRs, and latency expectations.

Next meeting
- Proposal: 30-minute NetOps-to-NetOps call next Tue/Wed to exchange account IDs and walk through the checklist.

Thanks again — Sean

--
Sean Gallagher
Senior AE, Redwood Inference
sean_gallagher@redwood.com | +1 415-555-0198

From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>

Date: Fri, 02 Apr 2027 16:12:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Post-demo: Private VPC connectivity recap & next asks

Copying internal network/ops notes here so we have a single source of truth.

Sean — great summary. A couple of technical clarifications for the ticket we should create: 
- For PrivateLink we need the customer AWS account ID + the target subnet(s) for the endpoint (these must be /26 or larger preferred).
- Ask about whether they use centralized NAT or per-AZ NATs. If centralized, we need the EIP ranges.
- Confirm if they require cross-region endpoints (adds complexity; we'll note in the SOW if so).

Internal asks to Dev (assignable):
- Can we provision a VPCE service in our dedicated account that maps to a service behind the LB (internal-only)? If yes, what is the expected lead time to enable in staging?
- Provide a short checklist for the NetOps call: needed fields are account ID, VPC ID, Subnet CIDRs, security group port list (we typically ask TCP 443), and preferred contact.

I’ll draft the HubSpot activity and open RDW-842 with these requirements. Attaching the redwood-connectivity-checklist.xlsx (stub) and will iterate after we get DataFoundry answers.

-Marissa

--
Marissa Cole
Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference

Hi Sean / Marissa — thanks for the clear recap. Confirming answers from our side: 

1) Preferred connectivity: PrivateLink. VPC peering is possible but we prefer not to expose broad routes across accounts.
2) AWS account ID for endpoint creation: 987654321000
3) Target subnets (we will create a dedicated subnet for the VPCE): us-west-2a: 10.10.64.0/26; us-west-2b: 10.10.65.0/26
4) NAT configuration: centralized NAT in the shared-services account — egress will appear from EIP range 54.219.120.0/28. If PrivateLink needs inbound, we will open SG accordingly.
5) NetOps contact: Priya Suresh <pri.suresh@datafoundry.com> (available M/W/F afternoons PST)

Attaching our network diagram (datafoundry-network-diagram.pdf) for reference.

We’d like Redwood to provision the VPCE service in staging first so our NetOps can test the handshake before production. Also, please send the DocuSign link for the connectivity addendum so procurement can get that processed this week.

Thanks — Alex

--

Perfect — thanks Alex and team for the details. Internal next steps and owners: 

1) RDW-842 (created) — Infrastructure: create VPCE service in staging and generate service name. Owner: Dev Patel. Due: 2027-04-06 EOD. Link: https://redwood.atlassian.net/browse/RDW-842
2) Security: provide expected SG rules and the service name we’ll give them to add to their SG outbound/peer allowlist. Owner: Marissa Cole. Due: 2027-04-05.
3) Sales: send DocuSign connectivity addendum to Alex. Owner: Sean Gallagher. Due: 2027-04-04.
4) NetOps-to-NetOps call: Target Tue 2027-04-06 10:00 PST — Marissa, please confirm availability and send calendar invite to Priya Suresh and netops-team@datafoundry.com.

Attachments: redwood-connectivity-checklist.xlsx (internal), I’ll copy the datafoundry-network-diagram.pdf into the ticket so infra has the topology.

Notes: For the allowlist ask, we typically supply the VPCE service name and request they allow outbound to our service network and TCP 443. If DataFoundry needs a fixed IP from our side we’ll discuss options (eg. NATing through a managed egress).

I’ll mark this as a priority for the Dedicated/Private path in the deal. Sean — please push the DocuSign link and I’ll coordinate the staging test with Dev.

Thanks — Lauren
